summary:
Moscow stands under the national framework of the Russian Federation, and the national assessment applies in the city. Documented enforcement in Moscow is prosecutorial and administrative: arrests on extremism charges, refusals of assembly permits, and registry practice.

Kotov, charged as the first person accused of creating an extremist organisation on LGBT grounds, was arrested in Moscow in late December 2024.

Moscow authorities have never approved a request to hold a gay pride rally in the city.

In 2011 the head of the Moscow Registry Office stated publicly that attempts by same-sex couples to marry in Moscow were "doomed to fail." The statement bears directly on a trans visitor whose relationship would be locally read as same-sex under birth-sex status.
tangentialFactors:
The Moscow prosecution of the first person charged with creating an extremist organisation on LGBT grounds extends enforcement from the display of symbols to the act of organising. Organising, rather than only visible expression, is the conduct charged in that case, and it is the framing that applies to anyone running or working with an LGBT group or venue in the city.

The city's own levers are administrative. Assembly permitting and marriage registration are handled at municipal level, while extremism prosecutions run through the national designation rather than a Moscow ordinance.
localsOnly:
For Moscow residents the practical closures are assembly and marriage registration. The city has never approved a gay pride rally, and the registry office's 2011 position was that marriage attempts by same-sex couples in Moscow would fail.

The first charge in the city for creating an extremist organisation on LGBT grounds was brought in late December 2024.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains no Moscow-specific figures on prosecutions, no municipal data on hate-crime recording, and no city-level documentation of police conduct, healthcare practice or custodial treatment.

The 2011 registry office statement is the most recent Moscow registry position in the sources; no later statement was identified, and whether permitting practice has changed since the sources were compiled is not established.
